analysis:
Scope: CI-only changes in .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml and .github/workflows/ci.yml. No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key-custody or release-signing code is touched, so TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 and TB-011 and the T-0xx provider threats are unaffected. The release pipeline and A-011 (binary hash registry) are not edited here.

Changes examined:
- Cache-write trust: a new SAVE_CACHES env, true only for push events on master or dev, is passed to the composite action as save-caches. Every actions/cache/save step (Swift build, SwiftPM repos, Metal, cluster metadata, MiMo audio codec, .git) is gated on it. Pull requests, including same-repo branches, now restore caches but never write them. This narrows the cache-poisoning surface relative to base, where PRs could save when nothing matched (base action.yml:91, ci.yml:~754). Restored caches are scoped by GitHub to the current, base or default branch, so PR code cannot seed what master restores.
- .git cache (new): .git is restored from cache, checked with git rev-parse and git fsck --connectivity-only, then actions/checkout runs. fsck --connectivity-only does not verify object contents or inspect .git/config or hooks. This is acceptable because only master and dev push runs write the cache, but it is a trust assumption on those pushes. persist-credentials: false keeps the job token out of the saved .git/config (ci.yml head ~lines 80-90). A restored .git could carry hooks or config from an earlier trusted push; PR jobs run after the restore and cannot persist changes.
- Sparse checkout excludes docs/reports/**/*.gz and landing mp4 files in every job except Docs Lint. This is a functional risk if other jobs read those paths, not a security issue.
- The SwiftPM repositories cache is keyed on a home-layout hash, lane and Package.resolved. Cache action versions stay SHA-pinned. The cluster key now drops git describe text.

No concrete regression was found. Unverified: the contents of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py and docs/developer/build.md#ci-caching, and whether any non-docs job reads the sparse-excluded paths. These do not affect the security conclusion.
